taxonomic_note: Species-level learner concept, distinct from the other Elymus species in this batch. Hybrids and infraspecific variants can blur characters; use an intact mature spikelet and do not force a hybrid/intermediate into either species.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: inspect the base of the glumes on an intact mature spikelet. Virginia wildrye commonly has pale, hard, conspicuously bowed-out U-like glume bases; the terminal spike is usually erect and comparatively compact, with shorter straighter awns than Canada wildrye.

best_field_traits: Tufted cool-season perennial with alternate leaf blades, jointed culms and a membranous ligule.
Terminal spike usually erect/straight, sometimes partially enclosed by the upper leaf sheath at its base.
Typically two multi-flowered spikelets at a rachis node.
Glume bases thickened, pale/bony and often strongly curved outward; high-value diagnostic structure.
Lemma awns relatively shorter and straighter than in E. canadensis; leaf width and habitat overlap.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Versus E. canadensis: glume bases usually pale, thickened and U-bowed, with a more erect, compact spike and shorter, less divergent awns. E. canadensis tends to nod with longer outward-spreading awns and glume bases that are not distinctly bowed. Intermediate plants and hybrids require additional examination.
